projects.title: YaraGen
projects.oneLine: Small, grammar-aware language models that write YARA malware-detection rules, scored for meaning with an SMT solver rather than string overlap.
bullets: With reasoning off, structured-trained Llama 3.1 8B and Ministral 3 8B beat GPT-5.4 and Sonnet 5 (reasoning on) few-shot on both Structured Logic → YARA and NL Prompt → YARA generation, and beat both zero-shot on rule repair.
Trained a 139M-parameter BART generator to 91.8% semantic correctness (93.7% in-window) on 22.7K held-out real-world rules, against 93.8% for a fully fine-tuned 8B model, at 17–20× the throughput.

Built the parts around it: the YaraAST hybrid tokenizer (+4 pp accuracy), Scooper, a 55M BiLSTM that masks IOCs behind placeholders (99.4% precision / 99.6% recall), and the Brownie & Puff evaluator (BLEU + compile + Z3 SMT) used as a training-time signal.

versus.label: Against frontier models
versus.note: Ours: structured-trained Llama 3.1 8B and Ministral 3 8B, reasoning off. Theirs: reasoning on. Next up: reasoning training and RLVR.

projects.caption: Scooper takes the IOCs out before generation and puts them back after, so a rule's length never depends on how long its indicators are.

projects.title: IOCScooper++
projects.oneLine: Pulls indicators of compromise and ATT&CK techniques out of real threat reports with a 50.6M-parameter model.
bullets: Trained ScooperNER-M (50.6M params) to 0.894 micro / 0.925 macro span-exact F1 on 47 held-out reports, beating fine-tuned encoder baselines 3–7× its size.
Extending extraction to grounded (entity, action, IOC) tuples mapped open-set onto all 637 ATT&CK techniques, with a co-annotated benchmark of real malware reports.
projects.caption: Dashed steps are Phase 2, in progress.

projects.title: AutoPYara
projects.oneLine: Generates YARA rules straight from malware binaries, grouped by family, and ships as a pip package.
projects.metricsNote: All vs. AutoYara, the prior state of the art.
bullets: Re-implemented and extended biclustering-based rule generation; benchmarked several clustering algorithms and heuristics for choosing K.
Beat AutoYara, the prior state of the art, on ≈71K samples collected over eight years.
projects.caption: Two estimates feed the generator: how many subclusters a family needs, and which samples sit at their centres.

projects.title: Ambiguity-Aware Research Agent

badges.text: Co-authored, 4-person team · led model development and training

projects.oneLine: Teaches a deep-research agent to ask one clarifying question when a query is underspecified, instead of answering the wrong question.
bullets: Fine-tuned Gemma-4-E4B (sparse MoE, ~9B total / ~4B active) through a four-stage SFT curriculum on one 80GB GPU, served with vLLM and multi-turn KV reuse.

Built a three-axis evaluation (detection, question quality, answer quality) with simulated users and LLM-as-judge; pause F1 rose from 0.168 to 0.573, while clarified answers still trail the no-pause baseline.
projects.caption: The open problem moved from deciding to ask to answering well after asking.

projects.title: Depixelation Recoverability Frontier
projects.oneLine: Measures exactly when pixelated text can be recovered, so redaction tools know where they fail.
bullets: Recasts depixelation from image restoration to constrained search with an exact render-and-verify check, over a 360-cell grid and a 10-seed protocol.
Scoping retrieval-augmented recognition with calibrated abstention and curriculum-training comparisons; framed defense-first.
projects.caption: A candidate only counts when re-pixelating it reproduces the sample exactly; the dashed exit is the abstention path still being scoped.

projects.title: Sturdy Fishstick
projects.oneLine: A job and PhD search platform that scrapes, scores and tracks listings with 1–2B models running locally.
bullets: Made 1–2B local models reliable judges by asking categorical questions (real job? level? field? skills overlap?) that map deterministically to a score, instead of asking for a number.
Ingested 6 ATS APIs with a Playwright fallback; grounded the chat in SQLite FTS5 so it cannot invent counts.
projects.caption: The small model only answers multiple-choice questions; the score itself is computed, never generated.

projects.title: HelloPentagon

badges.text: My part: detection models and backend design

projects.oneLine: An explainable malware detector: upload a Windows binary and get a verdict, its likely family, and a plain-language explanation for analysts.
bullets: Developed the malware-detection models: XGBoost and random-forest classifiers over PE and BODMAS features extracted from each upload.
Designed the backend: a Dockerized Flask API with SQLite, a hash-similarity family lookup, live Socket.IO alerts to the dashboard, and an LLM layer that explains each verdict.
projects.caption: The classifiers decide; the LLM only explains the verdict it is handed.

projects.title: Multiperspective Hawkeye
projects.oneLine: The ISCA'16 Hawkeye cache-replacement policy, implemented in zsim and extended.
bullets: Implemented Hawkeye in the zsim simulator and extended it with PC tracking and multi-policy benchmarking.
projects.caption: Hawkeye learns from what Belady's optimal policy would have done on past accesses, then predicts per load PC.

projects.title: Multimodal and VLM Evaluation
projects.oneLine: Measured a DeepSeek vision-language model against human-annotated ground truth.
bullets: Built the comparison harness and error analysis for object recognition and scene understanding.
projects.caption: Model output and human labels meet in one harness, and every disagreement goes to error analysis.
